Hi Erin / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the compliance path: 

Key constraints you shared
- Must sign BAA before any PHI leaves your network (controls gate for hosted/shared).
- External auditors will want access to retention policies, audit log extracts, and encryption key handling (KMS/HSM) for the inference layer.
- Expected timeline: security review this month, exec approval early November.

Redwood hosting options mapped to your asks
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, but requires BAA + evidence that we isolate PHI via tokenization/prefix filtering. We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and redwood_evidence_matrix.xlsx mapping to your questionnaire, but you indicated that HaaS (multi-tenant hosted) may not meet your legal team without additional contractual assurances.
- Dedicated Capacity (reserved GPU pool): provides tenant isolation at the serving layer and easier audit sampling; still managed by Redwood but we can provide isolated audit exports and dedicated log streams.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): highest assurance — customer-managed VPC or on-prem package; full audit trail under your control; recommended if legal requires on-prem handling of keys or air-gapped processing.

Immediate asks / mutual action plan
1) Erin/Tom: please share your security questionnaire PDF (we mentioned a short form you can use) — we can map answers directly in the attached evidence matrix.
2) Redwood: Marissa (SE) will validate which evidence we can provide for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and produce a gap list.
3) Redwood Security (Naomi) will prepare short notes on KMS/HSM options and logs retention windows.
4) Schedule: suggest a follow-up 30-min call Wednesday to review the gap list and decide whether to pursue Dedicated or Private given your legal timeline.

Attachments: redwood_evidence_matrix.xlsx (draft) — I started mapping common SOC2/BAA asks to the platform artifacts.
